Tohsaka says nothing.

Archer is nowhere to be seen, and Rider has vanished as well.

Tohsaka and I are alone in the church, waiting for Kotomine to appear.

“——Tohsaka.”

I call to her without rising from my seat.

“What?”

“There's something I need to ask you.”

“…I thought there might be. Fine. I'll tell you. There's no point hiding it anymore—and no reason left to.”

“You want to ask about Sakura?”

pages.en:
“——It began a long time ago. The Matou bloodline was thinning, and the children born into it possessed less and less magical energy… fewer and fewer Magic Circuits.

“The Matou were mages from a foreign land to begin with. Perhaps the soil of Japan simply didn't agree with them.

“Their decline began after they put down roots in this town. By the time the succession reached Shinji, the heir of the present generation, their Magic Circuits had disappeared altogether.”

pages.ja:
「……間桐の歴史はそれで終わったのよ。
間桐が追い求めたものを継承するだけなら、弟子でもなんでもとればよかった。けど間桐は名門だし、外部からの受け入れを拒否し続けた」

pages.en:
“…And with that, the history of the Matou came to an end.

“If all they wanted was someone to carry on their pursuit, they could have taken any apprentice. But the Matou were an ancient and prestigious family, and they refused to admit an outsider.”

pages.en:
“So the magical potential of each new heir declined, until at last the bloodline ran completely dry.

“…Only then did they try to find an apprentice. But no mage wanted to join a great house that had fallen into decay. The centuries-long history of the Matou—the Makiri—should have ended there.”

“——Now.

“Your household is unusual, so you may not know this, but a family of mages passes its art down to a single heir. Magecraft is never taught to any child but the chosen successor. Zouken told you that much, didn't he?

“If there are two siblings, one becomes the heir. The other is raised normally or given to another family.”

pages.en:
Some families might raise her without ever revealing their magecraft.

But that would be difficult, and inefficient besides.

After generations spent cultivating Magic Circuits through the bloodline, even a child who was not the heir would carry precious potential. Letting it lie dormant would run against everything a mage desired.

Then——

“…The declining Matou had no prospect of finding a suitable child to adopt.

“It was only natural that they would turn to the Tohsaka, whose family had been bound to theirs by an old alliance.”

“That was eleven years ago.

“After that, I was never allowed to meet her properly. It was part of the agreement with the Matou. She was their heir now, so I was told not to seek her out without cause.”

But at last I understand.

Why she was always asking after Sakura.

Why she refused to let Archer use his Noble Phantasm.

“…I'm glad. You're on Sakura's side, Tohsaka.”

A faint ray of light enters the stagnant darkness in my chest.

…I cannot imagine what will become of Sakura, or what any of us should do.

But on a road dark with nothing but foreboding, knowing that Tohsaka cares for her is enough to give me hope.

“Then I shall continue.

“The Crest Worms I described have eaten into Sakura Matou's nervous system.

“That is the result of eleven years spent growing inside her body. The worms have become nerves resembling Magic Circuits, spreading throughout her body as they entwine themselves with the nerves she was born with.

“The structures that have developed from those Crest Worms into a Magic Crest ordinarily lie dormant and exert no influence upon her.”

pages.en:
“But once activated, they invade Sakura Matou's nerves and continue moving, feeding upon her magical energy.

“That was what you witnessed earlier. The Crest Worms roamed through her body and stole away the magical energy that sustains her life.”

“Had that condition continued for another half day, Sakura Matou would have died.

“Once the Crest Worms exhaust the magical energy that powers them, they seek further nourishment in Sakura Matou herself. After draining her magical energy dry, the living crest will claim her flesh as well.”

“You possess a Magic Crest, so you should understand the magnitude of that pain.

“The human body protests at a foreign object no larger than a fingernail, sometimes so violently that life itself is impaired. Imagine alien nerves threaded through every part of your own, and then imagine the revulsion when those nerves begin to move. The nausea alone might be enough to kill.”

“Perhaps she possesses extraordinary will, or perhaps she has grown accustomed to the activation of the Crest Worms. Only she could tell us.”

How could I possibly understand?

Inserting a single Magic Circuit leaves my entire body drenched in sweat.

Sakura has many times that number.

Her pain is not something a person like me has any right to imagine casually.

pages.en: “…Wait. You said *once activated.* Are the Crest Worms ordinarily inactive?”

I suppress that selfish fury.

“What condition?”

I urge him toward the heart of the matter.

“Sakura Matou collapsed, and Rin attempted to save her. Rider prevented her, did she not?

“Then the condition is evident: abandoning her participation in battle as a Master. That must be the restriction placed upon the Crest Worms.”

“*What are you doing?*

“*You are a Master. Hurry and kill.*

“*If you cannot, we will devour you instead*——or words to that effect.”

“If she severs her contract with Rider by her own hand, the worms will devour Sakura Matou in earnest.”

“You, Rin, should understand the insanity of such a thing.”

“…I do. Mine should have integrated by now, but there are still times when I want to tear the whole arm off.

“And mine is confined to my left arm. If her entire body is filled with a crest, it will erode her ability to function as a human being.

“That isn't a mage. It's a mass of Magic Circuits. The human mind, housed in nothing more than the brain, can be rewritten by waves of magical energy.”

“Then——then Sakura…”

“She is in grave danger if her condition persists.

“I cannot say how many days she has. With every passing day, the Crest Worms will spread. Unless they can be removed before they reach every part of her body, she will die—but in all likelihood, her body will fail before then.”

“Thus far, I have only cleansed her body.

“The operation to restore her lost magical energy and recall her mind has yet to begin, and its chances of success are poor.

“——That is all.

“In conclusion, Sakura Matou cannot be saved as matters stand. Does that satisfy you, Shirou Emiya?”

“I understand the general situation, Kirei. I suppose I should thank you.”

She inclines her head without the slightest show of gratitude, then faces the priest again.
